slides.title: What is an Exception?
slides.content: An exception is a runtime error that disrupts the normal flow of a program. C# uses try, catch, finally, and throw to handle them gracefully.
slides.exampleOutput: Index was outside the bounds of the array.

options: A runtime error that disrupts program flow
exercise.answer: A runtime error that disrupts program flow

slides.title: Try-Catch Blocks
slides.content: The try block contains code that may throw. Catch blocks handle specific or general exceptions.

exercise.prompt: Choose the correct keyword to start an exception-handling block.

slides.title: Multiple Catch Blocks
slides.content: You can stack multiple catch blocks to handle specific exception types before the general Exception catch.
slides.exampleOutput: Illustrative sketch (contains placeholders); not directly executable.

exercise.prompt: In which order should catch blocks appear?

slides.title: Finally Block
slides.content: Finally runs whether an exception occurs or not. Use it for cleanup like closing connections or files.
slides.exampleOutput: Reads or writes a file; output depends on file contents.

slides.title: Throwing Exceptions
slides.content: Use 'throw new ExceptionType(...)' to raise an exception. You can also rethrow inside a catch block.
slides.exampleOutput: Declaration or expression only; produces no console output.

slides.title: Custom Exceptions
slides.content: Create custom exceptions by inheriting from Exception. Provide constructors that forward messages to the base class.
slides.exampleOutput: Class definition; produces no console output.

exercise.prompt: Complete the custom exception class declaration.

slides.title: Rethrowing and Stack Traces
slides.content: Use 'throw;' inside catch to preserve the original stack trace. Avoid 'throw ex;' unless you intentionally want to reset the stack trace.
slides.exampleOutput: Declaration or expression only; produces no console output.

exercise.prompt: Which preserves the original stack trace when rethrowing?

slides.title: Exception Best Practices
slides.content: Catch only exceptions you can handle. Use specific exception types. Do not swallow exceptions silently.
